title: Signature Commons Trust Charter
body:
A Signature commons trust charter declares a shared resource held for all members, names a steward, and fixes a distribution rule before any revenue arrives.

Signature design. The charter works in three clauses: the resource clause names what is held in common, the steward clause names who manages it and how they report, and the distribution clause states who receives what share of earnings. No clause may be changed without a public reading of the change and a waiting period, so members always know the rules they live under. The demo prints a charter for an example commons with its three clauses.

Use and limits. Use this charter as a template for any group holding a resource in common. Do not use it as a legal document, because it is a design template, not a filed charter.

Design detail. The charter's waiting period for changes is its most protective clause, because a trust is most vulnerable not when it is founded but when it is quietly amended. A proposed change must be read aloud at a public meeting, posted in writing for a fixed period, and then voted on, so that no member learns of a change only after it has taken effect. The steward's reports follow the same discipline: a quarterly statement of holdings, earnings, and distributions, written so that a member without financial training can check the arithmetic. A trust run this way can survive disagreements, because the rules for changing the rules are themselves trustworthy.

title: Signature Severance Share Calculator
body:
A Signature severance share calculator takes an extracted value, applies a community share rate, and splits the share between a present fund and a future fund.

Signature design. The calculator's rule is fixed: a share rate agreed in advance, a split agreed in advance, and no discretionary adjustment after extraction. The demo runs one extraction through the calculator and prints the present share, the future share, and the producer's remainder.

Use and limits. Use this calculator to teach how severance sharing works. Do not use it as a tax filing tool, because real severance taxes follow statutes, not templates.

Design detail. The calculator's fixed split exists because a share negotiated after extraction is always negotiated under pressure, when the producer wants to keep the revenue and the community wants to spend it. A rate and a split agreed before extraction remove that pressure: the producer knows the cost before digging, the community knows its share before spending, and the future fund receives its portion without an annual fight. The calculator prints all three numbers together, present share, future share, and producer remainder, so that no party can quote one number while hiding the others, and the present fund's spending is published alongside the future fund's balance.

title: Signature Fishing Quota Board
body:
A Signature fishing quota board posts the season's total catch, each fisher's share, and the remaining catch in one public table updated after every landing.

Signature design. The board's rule is transparency: every landing is entered the day it happens, the remaining catch is recomputed at once, and the season closes automatically when the remaining catch reaches zero. The demo posts a season total, three landings, and the remaining catch.

Use and limits. Use this board as a template for shared-stock management tools. Do not use it as a fisheries enforcement system, because real quotas need real science and real officers.

Design detail. The quota board's automatic closure is its key feature, because a season that closes on a decision can be extended by pressure, while a season that closes on arithmetic cannot. When the remaining catch reaches zero, the board posts the closure and the season ends, and no landing after that post is counted as legal catch. The board also keeps a public record of every landing, so that a fisher who suspects another of exceeding a share can check the table rather than accuse on rumor. Transparency of this kind does not end arguments about quotas, but it moves them from accusations to arithmetic, which is a better ground for settling them.

title: Signature Water Sharing Ledger
body:
A Signature water sharing ledger records each user's diversion date, quantity, and purpose, and settles shortages by seniority, oldest diversion first.

Signature design. The ledger's shortage rule is mechanical: sort users by diversion date, satisfy each in order until the available water runs out, and print who receives water and who waits. The demo settles a shortage among three users and prints the result.

Use and limits. Use this ledger to teach prior appropriation. Do not use it as a water rights registry, because real rights are recorded by state agencies.

Design detail. The ledger's seniority rule is harsh by design, and the ledger does not hide that harshness. In a shortage, the youngest user receives nothing, and the ledger prints that zero plainly rather than spreading the shortage thinly across all users, because the seniority system is a promise that early investment in diversion will be honored. The ledger also records each user's purpose, so that a shortage debate can distinguish a household's drinking water from a field's irrigation water, and a community using the ledger can decide, openly, whether to keep strict seniority or to adopt a sharing rule for emergencies. The ledger supports either choice, but it requires the choice to be written down.

title: Signature Solar Easement Form
body:
A Signature solar easement form records the protected collector area, the shading limit, and the neighbors who agree to respect it, in plain words on one page.

Signature design. The form's fields are a sketch of the collector, a height limit for nearby growth and building, and a duration, and every party signs the same page so that no separate agreement can contradict it. The demo prints a completed example form with its fields.

Use and limits. Use this form as a template for solar access agreements. Do not use it as a recorded legal easement, because real easements must be filed under local law.

Design detail. The easement form's one-page limit is a design choice, not an accident. A solar easement that runs to many pages will not be read by the neighbors it binds, and an unread agreement is a future dispute waiting for a new building or a growing tree. The form therefore carries only what a neighbor needs to know: where the collector sits, how high growth and building may rise near it, and how long the protection lasts, with a sketch that shows the protected sunlight path. Anything more detailed belongs in a separate technical appendix, and the form states plainly that the appendix does not override the one-page agreement.

title: Signature Spectrum Block Auction
body:
A Signature spectrum block auction divides a frequency band into blocks, takes sealed bids, and awards each block to the highest bidder at the second-highest price.

Signature design. The second-price rule is chosen so that bidders bid their true value: winning at the runner-up price removes the incentive to shade a bid. The demo runs an auction for one block with three bids and prints the winner and the price paid.

Use and limits. Use this auction as a teaching model for spectrum allocation. Do not use it as a real auction mechanism, because real spectrum auctions use complex multi-round rules.

Design detail. The second-price rule's virtue is honesty, and its honesty can be shown in one example. A bidder who values a block at one hundred and bids one hundred pays only the runner-up bid, so bidding truthfully costs nothing extra, while a bidder who shades a bid downward risks losing a block they value more than the price. A bidder who inflates a bid risks winning at a price above their value if the runner-up also bid high. The demo's three bids show the mechanism working: the winner pays the second-highest bid, the losers pay nothing, and every bidder's best strategy is to state their true value, which is why the rule is used for teaching even where real auctions are more complex.

title: Signature Airspace Layer Map
body:
A Signature airspace layer map draws three bands over a property: a private low band, a shared drone band, and a public high band, each with its own rule printed beside it.

Signature design. The map's rule is that a flight is judged by the band it flies in: the low band follows property rules, the drone band follows registration and height rules, and the high band follows aviation rules. The demo prints the three bands and their rules.

Use and limits. Use this map to teach airspace layering. Do not use it as a legal opinion about any real flight, because drone rules change and vary by place.

Design detail. The layer map's drone band is drawn as a shared band precisely because it is where the most disputes arise. A drone at rooftop height is near enough to disturb a household and far enough from the ground to claim navigable airspace, so neither property rules alone nor aviation rules alone settle it. The map therefore gives the drone band its own rules, registration, height limits, and a duty to avoid hovering over private yards, and it prints those rules beside the band so that a drone operator and a homeowner read the same page. A map that showed only two bands would force every drone flight into a category it does not fit, which is how disputes harden.

title: Signature Fee Fairness Test
body:
A Signature fee fairness test compares a fee against the cost of the service it funds and flags any fee that exceeds twice the service cost for review.

Signature design. The test's steps are to list the service, total its cost, state the fee, and compute the ratio, and any ratio above the threshold is printed as flagged rather than passed. The demo tests three example fees and prints their verdicts.

Use and limits. Use this test as a template for reviewing public fees. Do not use it as a legal finding, because courts apply their own standards to fees.

Design detail. The fee test's threshold of twice the service cost is deliberately simple, because a test that needs an accountant to run will not be run by the citizens it is meant to serve. A fee at or below cost passes, a fee modestly above cost passes with a note, and a fee above twice the cost is flagged for review, which means a public explanation rather than an automatic repeal. The flagged fee may still be justified, for example where a fee also funds enforcement or reserves, but the justification must be written and published, so that a flagged fee cannot survive on habit alone. The test's power is therefore procedural: it forces an explanation, not a verdict.

title: Signature Carbon Ledger
body:
A Signature carbon ledger records each emitter's tons, multiplies by a price, and prints the total cost and the share returned to the community.

Signature design. The ledger's rule is that every ton is counted and every payment is shown, so that no emitter can hide emissions and no revenue can disappear. The demo ledgers three emitters and prints the total and the community share.

Use and limits. Use this ledger to teach carbon pricing. Do not use it as an emissions registry, because real emissions need real measurement.

Design detail. The carbon ledger's community share is printed beside the total cost for a reason: a carbon price that disappears into a general budget will be suspected of being a revenue device, while a price whose community share is published can be judged as climate policy. The ledger shows each emitter's tons and cost, the total collected, and the half returned to the community, so that any reader can verify that the price was collected and shared as stated. The ledger also keeps the price itself visible, because a carbon price hidden in fuel surcharges cannot change behavior: firms and households respond to a price they can see, and the ledger makes it seen.

title: Signature Land Value Assessor
body:
A Signature land value assessor splits a property's sale price into land and building parts using a fixed method: comparable vacant lots set the land value, and the building value is the remainder.

Signature design. The assessor's method is printed with every assessment, so that an owner can see exactly how the split was made and challenge any step. The demo assesses one example property and prints the split and the land-only tax.

Use and limits. Use this assessor as a teaching model for land value taxation. Do not use it as a real assessment, because real assessments follow statutes and professional standards.

Design detail. The assessor's published method matters more than any single assessment, because land value is always an estimate and estimates are always disputable. By stating that comparable vacant lots set the land value and that the building value is the remainder, the assessor gives an owner a specific point to challenge: the choice of comparables, the adjustment for location, or the arithmetic of the remainder. An owner who can challenge the method can accept or contest the result with reasons, while an owner given only a number can only accept or resent it. The assessor's transparency is therefore not a courtesy but the mechanism that makes the tax legitimate.

title: Signature Dividend Distributor
body:
A Signature dividend distributor takes a fund's earnings, reserves a share for the fund's growth, and divides the rest equally among all members.

Signature design. The distributor's rule is equal shares and public arithmetic: every member can recompute their dividend from the published earnings and the published member count. The demo distributes example earnings among example members and prints each share.

Use and limits. Use this distributor as a template for commons dividend tools. Do not use it as a payment system, because real payments need real accounts and controls.

Design detail. The distributor's equal shares rule is stated before any earnings arrive, because a distribution rule chosen after the money appears will favor whoever is in the room. Equal shares also simplify the arithmetic to the point where any member can verify it: earnings minus reserve, divided by members, equals the dividend, and the distributor prints all three numbers. The reserve exists so that the fund can grow and can survive a poor year without cutting dividends to zero, and its size is itself a published rule rather than a discretionary holdback. A distributor run this way turns a windfall into an institution, which is the point of a commons trust.

title: Signature Grazing Permit Card
body:
A Signature grazing permit card states the allotment, the animal count, the season, and the fee on one card carried by the permit holder.

Signature design. The card's rule is that grazing outside the card's terms is not permitted grazing at all, and the card is checked against the allotment's remaining capacity before it is issued. The demo prints a card and its fee total.

Use and limits. Use this card as a template for permit tools. Do not use it as a real grazing permit, because real permits are issued by land agencies.

Design detail. The permit card's carried form matters because grazing happens far from offices, where a ranger and a rancher meet on the range rather than at a desk. A card that states the allotment, the animal count, the season, and the fee lets that meeting settle in one look: the ranger checks the card against the animals present, the rancher shows compliance without a trip to town, and a dispute about terms is resolved by reading the card aloud. The card also states the allotment's capacity, so that a permit that exceeds capacity is visibly wrong before it is issued, rather than discovered after the range is damaged.

title: Signature Timber Sale Planner
body:
A Signature timber sale planner lists a stand's volume, its appraised price, its road cost, and its reforestation requirement, and prints whether the sale covers its costs.

Signature design. The planner's rule is that a sale that does not cover its costs is printed as below-cost, so that the subsidy, if any, is visible rather than hidden. The demo plans one example sale and prints its verdict.

Use and limits. Use this planner to teach timber sale accounting. Do not use it as a sale appraisal, because real sales need real foresters.

Design detail. The timber planner's below-cost verdict is printed in plain words because a subsidy hidden inside a sale is worse than a subsidy debated openly. A sale that loses money may still be justified, for example where it clears diseased trees or funds a road the public also uses, but the justification must be stated beside the verdict so that the public can judge it. The planner therefore prints revenue, road cost, and verdict together, and it keeps the reforestation requirement on the same page, so that a sale cannot be judged profitable by ignoring the cost of regrowing what was cut.

title: Signature Beach Access Sign
body:
A Signature beach access sign states the public boundary in plain words, marks the access path, and gives the tide line rule for the day.

Signature design. The sign's rule is that a visitor reading it knows exactly where public access runs and where private land begins, without needing a surveyor. The demo prints a sign for an example beach with its boundary and path.

Use and limits. Use this sign as a template for access signage. Do not use it as a legal boundary marker, because real boundaries are fixed by survey and law.

Design detail. The beach sign's tide line rule is stated for the day because the boundary it marks moves with the tide, and a sign that gave a fixed line would be wrong twice a day. The sign tells a visitor to stay below the day's high tide line, points to the access stairway, and names the public area in words a child can understand. A visitor who follows the sign is lawfully on the beach, and a homeowner who reads the same sign knows exactly where public passage runs, so that the sign prevents the arguments that arise when each side carries a different map in mind.

title: Signature Wind Lease Board
body:
A Signature wind lease board tracks a lease through its stages, area identification, environmental review, auction, construction plan, and operation, and prints the stage and its conditions at each step.

Signature design. The board's rule is that no stage may be skipped and no stage's conditions may be dropped at a later stage, so that a lease reaching operation still carries its earliest environmental conditions. The demo advances an example lease through its stages and prints the final condition list.

Use and limits. Use this board as a template for staged leasing tools. Do not use it as a real lease record, because real leases are issued by government agencies.

Design detail. The wind lease board's carried conditions are its memory: a bird survey required at the area stage still binds at the operation stage, a fishing notice promised at auction still binds after construction, and a decommissioning bond posted early still stands when the turbines age. Boards that drop early conditions are how projects lose public trust, because communities remember promises that developers forget. The board therefore prints the full condition list at every stage, and any proposal to drop a condition must be posted as a change with reasons, so that the project's history is visible to anyone who checks it.

This record is an original Signature design, labeled Signature throughout. It is not a claim about a public place, law, or product, and its demo is original code executed at build time. The design is placed on the teaching ladder at its stated rank so that a reader meets the simple version before the compounded version and the compounded version before the most complex one, and the demo exists so that the design's behavior can be checked by running code rather than by trusting a description. Each record's demo was executed at build time and its output captured exactly, so that a reader who runs the demo program receives the same output printed in the record, and any difference between the printed output and a fresh run is itself a signal that the record or the code has changed since it was built.
demo_code:
stages = ['Area identified', 'Environmental review', 'Auction', 'Construction plan', 'Operation']
conditions = ['Bird survey', 'Fishing notice', 'Decommissioning bond']
for s in stages:
    print('Stage: ' + s)
print('Conditions carried through: ' + ', '.join(conditions))
demo_output:
Stage: Area identified
Stage: Environmental review
Stage: Auction
Stage: Construction plan
Stage: Operation
Conditions carried through: Bird survey, Fishing notice, Decommissioning bond

title: Signature Identity Rights Card
body:
A Signature identity rights card lists a person's protected attributes, the uses that need consent, and the income from licensed uses, keeping the attribute and the income in separate columns.

Signature design. The card's rule is the separation the public record explains: the attribute column is never taxed, and only the income column is taxable, so that a reader can see at once what is protected and what is charged. The demo prints a card for an example person with one licensed use and its income.

Use and limits. Use this card to teach the attribute-versus-income distinction. Do not use it as a legal document about any real person, because its example is invented.

Design detail. The identity card's two columns exist because the most common confusion about identity is the confusion between an attribute and its income. A name is not money, a signature is not money, and DNA is not money, but a licensed name can earn money, a signed endorsement can earn money, and a consented genetic study can be funded with money, and the tax law follows the money rather than the attribute. The card keeps the attribute column untaxed and the income column taxable, and it lists the consent that authorized each licensed use, so that a reader can see both what is protected and what was agreed, which is the whole of the identity question in one view.
